newsitem.title: ITALY: POLL-Italy July PSBR seen less than 4.5 trln lire.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Italy July PSBR seen less than 4.5 trln lire.

text.p: Italy's July state sector borrowing requirement is expected to be less than 4.5 trillion lire ($2.6 billion), less than half the 11.8 trillion needed in July 1996, analysts polled by Reuters said.

They attributed the sharp drop to the government's continuing tight rein on spending, a first slice of revenue from an advance tax on employees' severance pay and record high taxes paid to the Treasury by the Bank of Italy.

The consensus of analysts polled was for a monthly deficit of 4.4 trillion lire, which would take the cumulative January-July borrowing requirement to 29.8 trillion lire compared with 63.6 trillion for the first seven months of 1996.

Analysts said the deficit trend appeared in line with Italy's aim to achieve the three-percent deficit-to-gross domestic product (GDP) goal for European economic and monetary union (EMU), as stated in the Maastricht Treaty.
Italy's borrowing requirement in the first half was roughly 25.4 trillion lire, down from 53.75 trillion in first half 1996.
The government's 1997 target deficit is 58.7 trillion lire to reach the Maastricht Treaty's 3.0-percent target.
Giuliano Gasparini of Prometeia predicts an August deficit of 5.0 trillion lire against 11.0 trillion a year ago, the Treasury will be able to confirm it had more than halved borrowing needs.

But though expectations of reaching the 3.0-percent goal were more optimistic, Chiara Manenti of Caboto securities house cuationed that the September-December period still had to be faced. Manenti said that was "a period in which some 42/43 percent of annual spending is concentrated."
Economists saw Italy's public administration net debt at the end of 1997 at just under 62.0 trillion lire, or some 3.1 to 3.2 percent of GDP.
The government has excluded any further corrective budgetary measures this year to reach the EMU goal.
